title: autotune: defaults for batching & caching, quantization profiles, unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add autotune defaults for batching and caching; include quantization profile presets; add unit economics dashboard and export tooling.
description: Motivation: reduce per-token inference cost and make sensible, safe defaults for new and existing deployments by combining autotuned batching/caching defaults, quantization profile presets, and first-pass unit-economics (UEcon) tooling that surfaces tradeoffs to operators. This PR implements three workstreams in one coordinated rollout: 1) server-side autotune defaults for batching and KV/prefix caching with sensible safety caps, 2) a curated set of quantization profiles (int8/4-bit variants) with runtime metadata to allow automatic model variant selection, and 3) UEcon tooling: dashboard panels + a lightweight export that connects cost-per-token estimators to real traffic distributions so teams can simulate the impact of different profiles. Summary of changes: introduce AutotuneDefaults config and selection logic, add cache-aware batching heuristics, add quant_profiles.yaml and runtime selection code, add backend APIs and frontend panels for UEcon, add CLI export (redwood-cli uecon export) and a policy flag that enables automatic profile routing. Checklist: - [x] Implement AutotuneDefaults with feature-flag gating - [x] Add quantization profile registry and compatibility table - [x] Add UEcon API and basic dashboard panels - [x] Extend routing to prefer quantized variants for eligible requests - [x] Unit and integration tests for selection logic - [x] Rollout plan and canary tests completed Changes are backwards-compatible by default; feature flags control the new autotune behavior. See migration notes below for opt-in/opt-out instructions.
commits: feat(autotune): add AutotuneDefaults config and server-side selector
feat(quant): add quant_profiles.yaml and runtime metadata for model variants
feat(uecon): add UEcon API endpoints and initial dashboard panels
fix(e2e): adjust canary assertions for cache warm-up timing
chore(cli): add 'redwood-cli uecon export' for traffic simulation
review_comments: Diego Ramos: Overall LGTM but please add a migration note for Dedicated customers who pin GPU types; quant selection could pick incompatible variants.
Maya Chen: Added compatibility table to quant_profiles.yaml and unit tests to validate variant selection against pinned hardware.
Asha Patel: Can we limit automatic routing to the 'canary' tier initially? Concerned about tail-latency regressions.
Maya Chen: Implemented 'autotune.routing.policy' with 'safe' default and 'aggressive' opt-in; updated rollout plan.
Liam O'Connor: Integration tests flaked once due to cache warm-up; suggestion to add a deterministic warm-up in tests.
Maya Chen: Added deterministic warm-up hook for tests and retriggered CI. All checks passed afterwards. Approved-by: Diego Ramos, Asha Patel.
testing_notes: Local: run 'make dev-runtime' then 'go test ./services/runtime/... -run TestAutotuneSelector'
Integration: tests/integration/uecon_flow.test.js validates end-to-end selection and UEcon export
Canary: deployed to us-west-2/canary namespace for 72h, observed 11% cost reduction on low-context generation workloads with 0.3% median latency regressions that are within SLOs
rollout_plan: Step 1: feature-flag default off in main; enable in canary for 2 clusters
Step 2: monitor UEcon dashboard metrics and latency SLOs for 72h
Step 3: enable 'safe' policy for 25% traffic for teams that have not opted out
Step 4: after 2 weeks, evaluate and expand to 60% then global if metrics are stable
Rollback: disable feature flag and revert routing table; automated fallback to model variants without quantization
migration_notes: Dedicated customers who pin GPU families: quantized variant selection will not be applied unless the variant is marked compatible in quant_profiles.yaml
Customers with strict latency SLOs: set 'autotune.routing.policy' to 'manual' to keep current behavior
CLI: 'redwood-cli uecon export --help' explains how to simulate historical traffic against different profiles
